title: Coherence / fluency judge for memory-injected responses
summary: benchmarks/agent_quality/coherence.py: a 1-5 scale judge on whether injecting retrieved memory (via search()/get_context_card()) degrades response coherence or fluency vs. a no-memory control, even when the underlying fact is correct.
description:
None of this repo's existing metrics can detect a response that is factually right but reads as garbled, contradictory, or disjointed because of how retrieved memory was spliced into the prompt (e.g. `get_context_card()`'s per-type minimum-result balancing, from EPIC-7's Oracle 26.6-inspired work, injecting several memory types into one prompt) — a real risk this repo has designed for retrieval breadth but never scored for downstream text quality. Implement `benchmarks/agent_quality/coherence.py`: judge, on Microsoft's 1-5 coherence/fluency scale, the generated response's logical structure and grammatical quality under two conditions — with memory context injected (via `search()` or `get_context_card()`, matching whichever the question's suite uses) and a no-memory control answering from the question alone. Report the delta, not just the with-memory absolute score, since the interesting finding is whether memory injection specifically degrades quality, not the model's baseline writing quality.

Run this over the same BM-18 question set AGQ-3 uses so all Suite 4 judge dimensions share one evaluation pass rather than three separately-seeded runs that could disagree for reasons unrelated to the metric itself.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Judge prompt and 1-5 scale documented and version-pinned, same discipline as AGQ-3.
- Reports both absolute with-memory coherence/fluency scores and the delta vs. the no-memory control, per LongMemEval category.
- If `get_context_card()`'s multi-type injection shows a measurably larger coherence drop than single-type `search()` results, that finding is called out explicitly — this is the concrete hypothesis this story exists to test, not an incidental side note.

**Definition of Done:**
- `coherence.py` merged with mocked-judge unit tests, same pattern as AGQ-3.
- Results appended to BENCHMARKS.md Suite 4. Depends on AGQ-1 and EPIC-16's BM-18. Independent of AGQ-2/AGQ-3.
